Cars can perform the same melee animation in the account, but the window is tighter and the collision risk higher — the bike is the recommendation.
Single-source coverage: if your experience differs, trust the game — the description's wording ('melee drive-by') is the firm ground.
The trophy pops as the pedestrian goes down from the melee hit.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder a cumulative $250,000 of marked bills through your contacts. Marked bills come from heists, vaults and gang operations; laundering converts them at a cut, and the counter tracks the gross amount washed.

steps.text: Marked bills are the dirty cash from the Cartel Heist, bank vaults and gang operations — they cannot be spent until a contact launders them.
Laundering runs through contacts met in the story and strands: deliver marked bills, wait out the wash cycle, collect clean money minus their cut.
The counter tracks the total value put through the wash, not the clean amount returned — the cut does not slow the trophy.
Bank vaults are the steadiest marked-bill source after the story; Maximum Withdrawal's five vaults are a strong down payment on this total.
Gang operations pay in marked bills too, so Pest Control's nine hits feed this counter on the way past.
Do not sit on marked cash: it earns nothing in a stash, and the wash cycle takes in-game time, so keep the pipeline moving in parallel with other cleanup.
Higher-tier contacts wash larger batches at once — unlock them through the strand work and the cycle stops being the bottleneck.
Tick progress in the counter widget here in round thousands; the game surfaces laundered totals only at each wash's completion.
This is a late trophy by design: $250,000 of marked bills is several vaults and operations beyond the story's own supply.
The trophy pops when the cumulative washed total crosses $250,000.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend a cumulative $100,000 in shops — any shops, any goods. It accumulates quietly behind everything else you buy; if it lags late, vehicles and property-adjacent spending close it fast.

steps.text: Every shop purchase counts: clothes, weapons, ammo, vehicle work, food, fees and services — the counter is a lifetime spending total across all of them.
Ordinary play carries most of it: a full campaign with upgrades and garages typically lands within sight of the total by the finale.
Do not hoard for this one — money spent here is gone, but almost everything worth buying also serves another trophy.
Vehicle purchases and upgrades are the biggest single levers if you need a late push; one premium car can close a five-figure gap.
Garage properties themselves are Little Boxes' business; the fittings and services around them still count here.
Ammunition and armour restocks between endgame scores are a steady drip — top up fully rather than minimally and the total climbs.
The counter widget here tracks to $100,000; update it from the in-game stats page's spending line when you check your progress.
Spending marked bills is impossible until laundered — only clean-money purchases count, which is automatic in practice.
There is no deadline or decay: the total only rises.
The trophy pops as your cumulative shop spending crosses $100,000.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Buy all eight garage properties across Leonida. They unlock for purchase across the story; the set is a money trophy in disguise, so it lands naturally in the free-roam stage once income peaks.

steps.text: There are eight purchasable garages spread across the state, each appearing as a property marker once its area and story beat are reached.
Buy them as they unlock if cash allows — garages are also storage, and owned storage makes the vehicle work easier long before this trophy completes.
The full set costs serious money; the endgame economy (vaults, operations, laundering) is sized to fund it, which is why guides schedule it last.
Property purchases are permanent and cannot be sold back — but none of the eight is a trap; all are ordinary garages in useful places.
Tick each purchase in the counter widget here; property markers vanish after purchase, and the widget is the cleaner tally.
Two garages sit in late-opening areas — if you are stuck at six, story or area unlocks, not money, are the gate.
Buying property contributes to the 100% property share as well as this trophy.
Keep purchases in clean money; the funds from laundering are exactly what this set is designed to absorb.
There is no maintenance or upkeep cost that can repossess a garage — bought is bought.
The trophy pops on completing the purchase of the eighth garage.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register ten vehicles in the Scooter Bros app — the in-game vehicle registry you meet early. Registration is a phone action on vehicles you own or drive; ten distinct vehicles finish it. A second detailed account (Push Square) now covers the same system from the workshop side; where the two accounts differ, the disagreement note shows both.

steps.text: The Scooter Bros app is the phone's vehicle registry: while in a vehicle you own or have taken, open the app and register it to add it to your list.
Ten different vehicles are needed — registering the same car twice does nothing, so spread registrations across models.
Registration is free and instant; the only cost is remembering to do it when you take something new.
Pair it with Whip It Good: every time a discovery prompt fires for a new model, register that vehicle on the spot and both counters move together.
Story loaners and strand vehicles can be registered while you have them — Billy's bike and the heist cars are easy early entries.
Registered vehicles can be located and delivered through the app afterwards, which quietly makes cleanup travel faster.
The counter widget here tracks registrations; the app itself lists them if you want to check which models you already have.
Two detailed accounts now cover the details — the app flow above follows the first, the workshop account is added in the final step, and both are cross-checked against the official description.
There is no time pressure: vehicles registered at any point, in any order, all count.
The trophy pops as the tenth vehicle is registered.

Push Square's account adds the workshop side: a vehicle is registered at a Pay 'N' Spray or Mod Shop while you are driving it, the fee varies with the vehicle's value, and the registration needs an empty parking spot — the garages of Little Boxes are how you hold more spots.

trophies.disagree_note: How do you register, and does it cost anything? The first thorough account describes a free, instant phone action on a vehicle you are driving. Push Square's guide describes registration at a Pay 'N' Spray or Mod Shop, with a fee that varies with the vehicle's value and an empty parking spot required. Both agree on the substance — ten different vehicles, registered while you have them — so budget a little cash and keep a parking spot free, and either flow completes the set.
